overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 20
overview.text: In Lesson 19, students learned how to write the formulas for the graphs of parent functions (including quadratic, square root, and cube root) that were translated up, down, right, or left by k units. In this lesson, students extend what they learned in Module 3 about how multiplying the parent function by a constant or multiplying the x-values of the parent function results in the shrinking or stretching (scaling) of the graph of the parent function and, in some cases, results in the reflection of the function about the y- or x-axis. In this lesson, we will review some of Module 3's work with quadratic functions but will focus on cubic, square root, and cube root functions.
outcomes: Students recognize and use parent functions for absolute value, quadratic, square root, and cube root to perform transformations that stretch and shrink the graphs of the functions. They identify the effect on the graph of y=f(x) when f(x) is replaced with kf(x) and f(kx), for any specified value of k, positive or negative, and identify the constant value, k, given the graphs of the parent functions and the transformed functions. Students write the formulas for the transformed functions given their graphs.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 20 Exit Ticket: Stretching and Shrinking Graphs of Functions
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

How would the graph of f(x)=\sqrt{x} be affected if it were changed to g(x)=-2\sqrt{x}?

Sketch and label the graphs of both f and g on the grid below.
exitTicket.solution:
How would the graph of f(x)=\sqrt{x} be affected if it were changed to g(x)=-2\sqrt{x}?

The graph of f would be stretched vertically by a factor of 2 and reflected across the x-axis.

Sketch and label the graphs of both f and g on the grid below.

y=f(x)y=g(x)y=f(x)y=g(x)

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Master Stretching and Shrinking Graphs of Functions through authentic curriculum practice problems. Check your work using the expandable teacher solution key below.

problems.prompt: Graph the functions in the same coordinate plane. Do not use a graphing calculator.

g(x)=2|x|

h(x)=|3x|

k(x)=-3|3x|

Explain how the graphs of functions j(x)=3|x| and h(x)=|3x| are related.
problems.solution: Each of these transformations of the absolute value functions creates the same graph.

problems.prompt: Explain how the graphs of functions q(x)=-3|x| and r(x)=| -3x| are related.
problems.solution: The two graphs have the same scaling factor of 3, but they are reflections of each other across the x-axis. Multiplying an absolute value by a negative number will reflect it across the x-axis. However, multiplying by a negative number INSIDE the absolute value has the same effect as multiplying by a positive number on the outside.

problems.prompt: Write a function, g ,in terms of another function, f, such that the graph of g is a vertical shrink of the graph f by a factor of 0.75.
problems.solution:
g(x)=0.75 f(x)

MP.3MP.3In Problem 5, students critique the reasoning of each answer, determine which of the two is correct, and provide a justification for their response.

problems.prompt: A teacher wants the students to write a function based on the parent function f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}. The graph of f is stretched vertically by a factor of 4 and shrunk horizontally by a factor of \frac{1}{3}. Mike wrote g(x)=4\sqrt[3]{3x} as the new function, while Lucy wrote h(x)=3\sqrt[3]{4x}. Which one is correct? Justify your answer.
problems.solution: Mike is correct. A vertical stretch by a factor of 4 means multiplying f(x) by 4, and a horizontal shrink by a factor of \frac{1}{3} means that the x-values of f(x) must be multiplied by 3.

problems.prompt: Study the graphs of two different functions below. Which is a parent function? What is the constant value(s) multiplied to the parent function to arrive at the transformed graph? Now write the function defined by the transformed graph.
problems.solution:
y=f(x)y=g(x)y=f(x)y=g(x)

The parent function is f(x)=\sqrt{x}. The graph of y=g(x) is the graph of y=f(x) reflected across the x-axis. The function depicted by the transformed graph is g(x)=-\sqrt{x}.
